creator: Alexander Terp
description:
A single typo produces one diagnostic per error node in the tree, so
the user reads the same mistake described two or three times.

    $ printf 'bad syntax here!!!\n' | rad -
    error[RAD10009]: Unexpected 'bad syntax here!!!'
      --> t.rad:1:1
    error[RAD10009]: Unexpected '!!!'
      --> t.rad:1:16

Noticed while building the REPL (RED-11), where it stings more than in
a script: you see it on every mistyped line rather than once before
exiting. The REPL borrows its syntax diagnostics from the checker
precisely so the two paths agree, so this is one behavior in two
places, not two bugs.

Likely fix: report only the outermost invalid node, dropping nested
ones whose span is contained by an ancestor's. Worth checking whether
any existing case genuinely wants the inner report - two unrelated
errors on one line should still produce two.

Touches rts/check (where the diagnostics come from) and will churn
snapshots in core/testing and rts/check.
title: One syntax error prints several diagnostics
